title: Private deployments follow-up: SIEM audit export constraints + GA roadmap spike
creator: Ethan Park
body:
## Context
Beta scope for SIEM-ready audit export is Hosted + Dedicated (Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs, and S3 delivery). Multiple enterprise prospects (and at least one procurement thread) are asking whether the feature will work for Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on-prem / air-gapped). This spike documents constraints, identifies viable integration patterns, and proposes a GA roadmap plan.

Primary references:
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/siem-ready-audit-export-beta-prd.json
- Audit schema v2 + SIEM mapping: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-event-schema-v2-and-siem-mapping.json
- Delivery semantics ADR: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-audit-export-delivery-semantics-and-idempotency.json
- Filtering model ADR: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-audit-export-filtering-model.json
- Exporter service architecture: sources/confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/audit-exporter-service-architecture.json

## Goals
1) Enumerate constraints for Private (VPC-connected) and on-prem/air-gapped deployments.
2) Decide what is feasible for GA without over-expanding the exporter scope.
3) Recommend a delivery model(s) that preserve:
   - at-least-once delivery + checkpointing
   - least-privilege RBAC for config + credential rotation
   - encryption-in-transit/at-rest and PII minimization
   - operational visibility (lag, errors, destination health)

## Non-goals
- Implement Private support in this ticket.
- Negotiate customer-specific network exceptions.
- Design a net-new audit event schema (we assume schema v2 is canonical).

## Deployment variants considered
A) Private (VPC) – Redwood-managed control plane + customer VPC connectivity (typical “Private” posture)
B) Private (VPC) with very restricted egress (allowlist-only outbound, central proxy required)
C) On-prem connected (customer DC with outbound allowed via proxy/VPN)
D) On-prem air-gapped (no outbound connectivity; sometimes no inbound except customer admin)

## Findings / constraints
### 1) Network + egress constraints dominate
- Many Private customers require outbound egress to be explicitly allowlisted and routed through a customer-managed proxy. This affects:
  - Splunk HEC (destination may be internal, which is good) OR may be Splunk Cloud (requires outbound Internet).
  - Datadog intake (almost always Internet) → likely not viable for strict Private.
  - S3 delivery: frequently cross-account buckets in the customer’s cloud account; may require STS assume-role and explicit endpoint policies; in Private, the S3 endpoint may be via VPC endpoints rather than public Internet.
- Air-gapped customers generally cannot use “push to Internet” destinations at all. They prefer either:
  - push to an internal SIEM endpoint (Splunk indexers on-prem, syslog relays, internal object store)
  - or pull-based extraction (customer pulls from a local store / file drop)

### 2) Control plane dependency must be made explicit
Current beta architecture assumes:
- a Redwood control plane service owns export config CRUD + RBAC
- exporter service consumes config and exports events

For Private:
- If control plane is still reachable (Private VPC-connected), we can keep the config API in the control plane and run an exporter in the customer environment (or in Redwood-managed infra with VPC connectivity).
- For air-gapped, a “central control plane” model breaks down. We need a local control plane surface (or an offline config mechanism) that still provides:
  - audited config changes
  - safe validation
  - RBAC integration with the customer’s IdP (often via their SSO integration in Private)

### 3) Destination support should be reframed for Private
- Splunk HEC is the most Private-friendly because many customers run Splunk Enterprise or forwarders internally.
- S3 should be framed as “object storage delivery,” not strictly AWS S3:
  - Some on-prem customers use S3-compatible stores (MinIO, Dell ECS, Ceph RGW).
  - However, SSE-KMS semantics vary; we should be careful promising full parity with AWS KMS.
- Datadog Logs intake is low priority for Private/on-prem due to egress requirements.

### 4) Secrets and key management differ in Private
- Hosted/Dedicated: Redwood-managed secret storage and rotation flows.
- Private: customers expect secrets to be stored/managed in their environment:
  - Kubernetes secrets + external secrets operators (Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, GCP Secret Manager, Azure Key Vault)
  - Customer-managed KMS/HSM in regulated environments

We should avoid building bespoke secret managers into the exporter; instead, integrate with existing Private secret reference patterns.

### 5) Ops and observability expectations
Private customers often want metrics/logs in their own monitoring stack:
- Prometheus/Grafana scrape endpoints inside their network
- Log forwarding to their log system
- Minimal “phone-home” telemetry (or strictly opt-in)

We should plan for an “exporter metrics bundle” that can be deployed and scraped locally, and define the minimal required signals for support.

## Proposed GA roadmap
### Phase 0 (current beta): Hosted + Dedicated (keep scope)
No change. Continue to message “Private/on-prem out of scope for beta” (per PM).

### Phase 1 (GA target): Private (VPC-connected) support via same exporter, customer-managed egress
Recommended approach:
- Run audit-exporter in the same environment boundary as audit event storage/queue in Private.
- Keep config API and RBAC aligned with the Private control plane (same CRUD shape), but deployed into the Private control plane instance.
- Destinations for Phase 1:
  1) Splunk HEC (customer internal endpoint or Splunk Cloud via proxy)
  2) Object storage delivery to customer bucket (AWS S3 via VPC endpoint / cross-account role; optionally “S3-compatible” best-effort)
- Add explicit knobs for:
  - proxy configuration (HTTP(S)_PROXY / NO_PROXY; plus certificate chain management)
  - destination allowlisting (align with existing egress allowlist hooks added under threat model work)
- Observability:
  - local Prometheus metrics and dashboards
  - optional support bundle export (manual download) rather than automatic exfiltration

### Phase 2 (later GA / enterprise add-on): On-prem connected
Same model as Phase 1, but validate:
- proxy-only egress
- destination endpoints that are internal-only
- storage scaling with limited managed services (no managed queues)

This likely requires packaging work + SRE supportability review.

### Phase 3 (separate initiative): Air-gapped / offline
Do not bundle into SIEM export GA unless we explicitly staff packaging + support.
Two viable patterns to evaluate in a dedicated design:
1) **Local file/object-store staging + customer pull**
   - Exporter writes NDJSON (or parquet) batches to a local object store / filesystem with strong checkpointing.
   - Customer runs their own shipper (Splunk UF, Fluent Bit, custom) to pull and forward into SIEM.
   - Pros: avoids outbound egress; matches air-gapped reality.
   - Cons: changes the “delivery guarantee” boundary (Redwood guarantees staging, not final SIEM ingestion).
2) **Customer-hosted adapter / plugin model**
   - Redwood provides an SDK or plugin interface for a destination adapter that customers run in their network.
   - Pros: extensible for exotic sinks.
   - Cons: support burden; security review complexity.

Recommendation: Make Phase 3 a separate roadmap item with clear contract language and a “support boundary” doc.

## Open questions / risks
1) **Config plane for air-gapped:** Do we require a local Console/Control Plane to exist for Private on-prem already, or do we need a CRD/manifest-based config? (Platform Control Plane + Console input needed.)
2) **S3-compatible semantics:** If we claim compatibility, what’s the minimal contract (auth, TLS, multipart, encryption)? Might be better to label it “S3-compatible (best effort)”.
3) **Support boundaries:** For pull-based patterns, what language goes into SOC2/ISO evidence and security FAQ? (GRC + Legal input.)
4) **Dedup/idempotency:** At-least-once delivery remains, but for file staging, customer shippers may duplicate. Need clear downstream dedup guidance using event_id (already in ADR).

## Concrete recommendations (engineering)
- Treat Private (VPC-connected) as “same architecture, different packaging + network constraints.”
- Keep the destination set intentionally small for initial Private GA: Splunk HEC + S3/object storage.
- Add first-class proxy support and document required egress allowlists.
- Provide an offline “support bundle” collector that snapshots:
  - exporter config (redacted)
  - last checkpoints
  - recent error summaries
  - metric sample

## Outputs of this spike
- This ticket’s notes + a shareable roadmap summary for PM/Sales.
- Follow-up tickets proposed below.

## Follow-up tickets to file (proposed)
1) ENG-XXXX: Private packaging plan for audit-exporter (Helm/Kustomize + upgrade story)
2) ENG-XXXX: Proxy support + cert management for Splunk/S3 adapters in Private
3) ENG-XXXX: Object storage “S3-compatible” compatibility matrix + test harness
4) PM-XXXX: Define GA scope for Private + update security FAQ language

## Stakeholder review
- Platform Control Plane: Ethan Park (align on config/RBAC deployment model)
- Security Eng: Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei (PII + threat model deltas for Private)
- SRE: Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes (supportability, SLOs in customer env)
- Product: Naomi Feldman (scope and roadmap messaging)
comments: 2025-04-28 (Diego Santos): Kicked off spike. I’m going to split findings into (a) VPC-connected Private, (b) on-prem connected, (c) air-gapped. Will sync with Marcus on threat model deltas and with Sean on support boundaries (what we can reasonably page on if metrics live in customer env).

2025-05-02 (Marcus Lin): Biggest risk is accidental data exfil via misconfigured destinations in Private. We should require egress allowlist + destination validation to be enabled by default in Private builds, even if Hosted can be more permissive. Also: ensure support bundle is opt-in and redacts secrets + any actor metadata beyond what’s already in audit schema policy.

2025-05-06 (Sean Gallagher): +1 on treating air-gapped as separate initiative. For Phase 1 Private GA, we need a defined minimum: local metrics endpoint, health endpoint, and a standard “how to diagnose lag” doc. Without that, on-call will be blind. We should avoid any design that requires Redwood to reach into customer networks for debugging.

2025-05-09 (Ethan Park): For Private VPC-connected, we can deploy the same config CRUD service into the Private control plane instance. That’s the cleanest option versus inventing a manifest-based config. Air-gapped is a different story; likely needs CRDs or offline config import/export, but let’s keep it out of initial GA scope.

2025-05-15 (Naomi Feldman): This roadmap framing works for PM. Please make sure we explicitly call out Datadog as unlikely for Private due to egress and keep Splunk+S3 as the primary story. I’ll incorporate this into GA planning and the security FAQ update.
